title: The drone that saved 79 minutes… or 19 (compared to what?)

scenes.text: A blood-delivery drone saved 79 minutes. Or was it just 19? Both numbers come from the same study.
In Rwanda, a peer-reviewed study covered 12,733 drone blood orders to 20 hospitals.
The drone: a median of 41 minutes. The hospital's ambulance: 120, because it had to drive there and back. The gap: 79.
But against the best case, a car that only goes one way, about an hour, the gap shrinks to 19.
It's like saying you're tall. Next to whom?
And 67% less expired blood at 12 months. The fine print: no control group, estimated road times, and no cost per delivery.
So when you see a number, ask: compared to what? And check its evidence level, from A to D.
A number without its comparison is half a number.
Save it, and share it with someone who believes any number.
